import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.72

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is every variety of groups whose relatively free groups are residually
(torsion-free nilpotent) either soluble or the variety of all groups?

It would suffice for an affirmative answer to prove that every variety of Lie
algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ containing no finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra
is soluble.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.72»

/-- A variety of groups, presented by a set of identities in countably many variables. -/
abbrev GroupVariety := Set (FreeGroup ℕ)

/-- A group belongs to a variety when every evaluation of every defining identity is trivial. -/
def GroupVariety.Models (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ V, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- All substitutions in variables of type `α` of the identities defining `V`. -/
def GroupVariety.relators (V : GroupVariety) (α : Type*) : Set (FreeGroup α) :=
  {w | ∃ v ∈ V, ∃ f : ℕ → FreeGroup α, FreeGroup.lift f v = w}

/-- The relatively free group of rank `α` in `V`: the free group on `α`, modulo the verbal
subgroup generated by the identities of `V`. -/
def GroupVariety.relativelyFree (V : GroupVariety) (α : Type*) :=
  PresentedGroup (V.relators α)

instance (V : GroupVariety) (α : Type*) : Group (V.relativelyFree α) := by
  change Group (PresentedGroup (V.relators α))
  infer_instance

/-- A group is residually torsion-free nilpotent if every nonidentity element survives under a
homomorphism to some group which is both nilpotent and torsion-free. -/
def IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (N : Type) (_ : Group N),
    Group.IsNilpotent N ∧ IsMulTorsionFree N ∧ ∃ f : G →* N, f g ≠ 1

/-- A group variety is soluble if one fixed term of the derived series vanishes in every member. -/
def GroupVariety.IsSoluble (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Models G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥

/-- A group variety coincides with the variety of all groups if every group belongs to it. -/
def GroupVariety.IsAllGroups (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Models G

/--
Is it true that every variety of groups whose relatively free groups of every
rank are residually torsion-free nilpotent is either soluble, with a uniform
bound on derived length, or coincides with the variety of all groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety,
      (∀ α : Type, IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (V.relativelyFree α)) →
        V.IsSoluble ∨ V.IsAllGroups := by
  sorry

/-- A variety of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$, presented by a set of Lie identities in
countably many variables. -/
abbrev LieVariety := Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ)

/-- A Lie algebra belongs to a variety when every evaluation of every defining identity is zero. -/
def LieVariety.Models (V : LieVariety) (L : Type*) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L] : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ V, ∀ f : ℕ → L, FreeLieAlgebra.lift ℚ f p = 0

/-- A Lie variety is soluble if one fixed term of the derived series vanishes in every member. -/
def LieVariety.IsSoluble (V : LieVariety) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
    V.Models L → LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥

/-- The variety has no member which is both finite-dimensional and simple. Mathlib's notion of a
simple Lie algebra includes the requirement that it be nonabelian. -/
def LieVariety.HasNoFiniteDimensionalSimpleMembers (V : LieVariety) : Prop :=
  ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
    V.Models L → FiniteDimensional ℚ L → ¬ LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L

namespace variants

/--
Every variety of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ which contains no
finite-dimensional simple (in particular, nonabelian) Lie algebra is soluble,
with one uniform bound on the derived length of all its members.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17]
theorem lie_algebras :
    ∀ V : LieVariety, V.HasNoFiniteDimensionalSimpleMembers → V.IsSoluble := by
  sorry

end variants

end Kourovka.«4.72»
modeling_decisions: Represented a group variety by a set of identities in the countably generated free group. A group is a member exactly when every evaluation of every listed identity is trivial. Countably many variables suffice because each group term uses only finitely many variables.

Defined the relatively free group of rank α as the free group on α modulo the normal closure of all substitutions of the variety's identities. The main hypothesis quantifies over every α : Type, including rank zero.

Read “residually nilpotent torsion-free” as residually in the class of groups that are simultaneously nilpotent and torsion-free: every nonidentity element survives under a homomorphism to such a group.

Made “soluble variety” uniform: one fixed derived-series index annihilates every member. This encodes a solubility identity rather than merely requiring each member to have some member-dependent derived length.
Made “coincides with the variety of all groups” semantic (`every group models the identities`) rather than requiring a particular identity basis to be empty.

Represented a Lie variety over ℚ by identities in the countably generated free Lie algebra over ℚ. Excluded members satisfying both `FiniteDimensional ℚ L` and Mathlib's `LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L`, whose definition includes nonabelianness.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.72

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent
torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups? For an
affirmative answer, it is sufficient to show that every variety of Lie algebras over the
field of rational numbers which does not contain any finite-dimensional simple algebras
is soluble.

A variety of groups is a class of groups closed under subgroups, quotients and arbitrary
direct products. By Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups defined by
a set of laws, i.e. of words in the free group $F(x_0, x_1, \dots)$ on countably many
variables. We therefore represent a variety of groups by a set $S$ of laws: a group belongs
to the variety iff every word in $S$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution. The free
groups of the variety are its relatively free groups $F(X) / S(F(X))$, where $S(F(X))$ is
the verbal subgroup of the absolutely free group $F(X)$, for sets $X$ of every cardinality.
A variety is soluble if it satisfies a solubility law, i.e. if all its members are soluble of
some fixed derived length.

Varieties of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ are represented in the same way, by sets of laws
in the free Lie algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ on countably many variables.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.72»

-- ### Varieties of groups

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w ∈ F(x₀, x₁, …)` if `w` evaluates to `1` under every
homomorphism `F(x₀, x₁, …) → G`, i.e. under every substitution of elements of `G` for the
variables. -/
def Group.SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = 1

/-- The group `G` belongs to the variety of groups defined by the set of laws `S`. -/
def Group.MemVariety (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ S, Group.SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- The verbal subgroup `S(G)` of `G` determined by the set of laws `S`: the subgroup generated
by all values in `G` of the words in `S`. -/
def verbalSubgroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ S, ∃ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = g}

instance verbalSubgroup_normal (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    (verbalSubgroup S G).Normal := by
  let base : Set G := {g | ∃ w ∈ S, ∃ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = g}
  change (Subgroup.closure base).Normal
  suffices h_base : base = Group.conjugatesOfSet base by
    rw [h_base]
    exact Subgroup.normalClosure_normal
  refine Set.Subset.antisymm Group.subset_conjugatesOfSet fun a h => ?_
  simp_rw [Group.mem_conjugatesOfSet_iff, isConj_iff] at h
  rcases h with ⟨b, ⟨w, hw, f, rfl⟩, c, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨w, hw, (MulAut.conj c).toMonoidHom.comp f, rfl⟩

/-- The relatively free group on the set `X` of free generators in the variety of groups defined
by the set of laws `S`: the quotient of the (absolutely) free group `F(X)` by its verbal
subgroup `S(F(X))`. -/
abbrev RelativelyFreeGroup (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (X : Type*) : Type _ :=
  FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup S (FreeGroup X)

/-- A group `G` is residually torsion-free nilpotent if every non-trivial element of `G` remains
non-trivial in some torsion-free nilpotent quotient of `G`. -/
def IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal),
    g ∉ N ∧ Group.IsNilpotent (G ⧸ N) ∧ ∀ x : G ⧸ N, IsOfFinOrder x → x = 1

/-- The variety of all groups is defined by the empty set of laws. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem memVariety_empty (G : Type*) [Group G] : Group.MemVariety ∅ G :=
  fun _ hw => hw.elim

/-- In the variety of all groups, verbal subgroups are trivial, so the relatively free groups
are the absolutely free groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_empty (G : Type*) [Group G] : verbalSubgroup ∅ G = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- Commutative groups satisfy the commutator law `[x₀, x₁]`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaw_commutator_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] :
    Group.SatisfiesLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ := fun f => by
  rw [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  exact mul_comm _ _

/--
Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent
torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups?

Here a variety of groups is given by a set of laws $S \subseteq F(x_0, x_1, \dots)$, its free
groups are the relatively free groups $F(X) / S(F(X))$ for all sets $X$, "residually nilpotent
torsion-free" means residually (torsion-free nilpotent), and the variety is soluble if all its
members are soluble of some fixed derived length $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      (∀ X : Type, IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (RelativelyFreeGroup S X)) →
        (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Group.MemVariety S G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥) ∨
          ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Group.MemVariety S G := by
  sorry

-- ### Varieties of Lie algebras

/-- A Lie algebra `L` over `R` satisfies the law `w` in the free Lie algebra over `R` on the
variables `x₀, x₁, …` if `w` evaluates to `0` under every Lie algebra homomorphism from the free
Lie algebra to `L`, i.e. under every substitution of elements of `L` for the variables. -/
def LieAlgebra.SatisfiesLaw (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (L : Type*) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L]
    (w : FreeLieAlgebra R ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeLieAlgebra R ℕ →ₗ⁅R⁆ L, f w = 0

/-- The Lie algebra `L` over `R` belongs to the variety of Lie algebras defined by the set of
laws `S`. -/
def LieAlgebra.MemVariety (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S : Set (FreeLieAlgebra R ℕ)) (L : Type*)
    [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ S, LieAlgebra.SatisfiesLaw R L w

/-- Abelian Lie algebras satisfy the law `⁅x₀, x₁⁆`. -/
@[category test, AMS 17]
theorem LieAlgebra.satisfiesLaw_lie_of_isLieAbelian (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (L : Type*)
    [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L] [IsLieAbelian L] :
    LieAlgebra.SatisfiesLaw R L ⁅FreeLieAlgebra.of R 0, FreeLieAlgebra.of R 1⁆ := fun f => by
  rw [LieHom.map_lie, trivial_lie_zero]

/--
Every variety of Lie algebras over the field of rational numbers which does not contain any
finite-dimensional simple algebras is soluble.

Here a variety of Lie algebras over $\mathbb{Q}$ is given by a set of laws $S$ in the free Lie
algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ on countably many variables, "simple" means simple and non-abelian
(as in `LieAlgebra.IsSimple`), and the variety is soluble if all its members are soluble of
some fixed derived length $n$. The Kourovka Notebook records that this statement implies an
affirmative answer to `kourovka.«4.72»`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72».variants.lie_algebras :
    ∀ S : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ),
      (¬ ∃ (L : Type) (_ : LieRing L) (_ : LieAlgebra ℚ L),
          LieAlgebra.MemVariety ℚ S L ∧ FiniteDimensional ℚ L ∧ LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
          LieAlgebra.MemVariety ℚ S L → LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.72»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's readings (residually (torsion-free nilpotent); soluble variety = uniformly bounded derived length; Lie 'simple' = non-abelian simple as in Mathlib; only the Lie claim formalized for the second slot) are all consistent with the standard meaning of the Kourovka statement and were followed.
modeling_decisions: Varieties (of groups and of Lie algebras) are represented by arbitrary sets of laws in the countably generated free group / free Lie algebra rather than as HSP-closed classes; by Birkhoff's theorem the two notions coincide, and every law involves finitely many variables so FreeGroup ℕ / FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ suffice.

'Free groups of the variety' = relatively free groups F(X)/S(F(X)) for all X : Type (all ranks in universe 0); the property is in fact determined by the countable-rank one, so restricting to Type loses nothing.

'Residually nilpotent torsion-free' is read as residually (torsion-free nilpotent), as instructed by the table, using quotients G ⧸ N rather than homomorphisms to external groups (avoids universe issues; equivalent). Torsion-free is spelled out as 'every element of finite order is trivial' rather than Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree.

'Soluble variety' = ∃ n uniform with derivedSeries G n = ⊥ (resp. LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥) for all members; 'coincides with the variety of all groups' = every group (in Type) satisfies all laws of S. Quantifying members over Type only is harmless because laws are detected by the countable-rank relatively free group, which lives in Type.

'Finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra' uses Mathlib's LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L (non-abelian, no nontrivial ideals) together with FiniteDimensional ℚ L; the witness is quantified over L : Type, which is enough since every finite-dimensional ℚ-algebra is isomorphic to one in Type.
The Lie-algebra slot is stated as a definite Prop with category research open (as directed), and the implication to the group question is only mentioned in the docstring, not formalized.

Three small `category test` lemmas are included as API sanity checks for the bespoke definitions (empty set of laws = all groups; verbal subgroup of ∅ is ⊥; commutative groups / abelian Lie algebras satisfy the commutator law).

(torsion-free nilpotent) either soluble, with a uniform bound on derived length, or the variety of

namespace Kourovka.«4.72»

universe u

/-- An equational presentation of a variety of groups. An element of `V n` is a law in `n`
variables, represented by a word required to equal one. -/
abbrev GroupVariety := ∀ n : ℕ, Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))

namespace GroupVariety

/-- A group satisfies an equational presentation of a group variety if every law vanishes under
every substitution of its variables. -/
def Satisfies (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (w : FreeGroup (Fin n)), w ∈ V n →
    ∀ f : Fin n → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The verbal subgroup in the free group on `X` generated by all substitution instances of the
laws of `V`. -/
def verbalSubgroup (V : GroupVariety) (X : Type u) : Subgroup (FreeGroup X) :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {x | ∃ (n : ℕ) (w : FreeGroup (Fin n)), w ∈ V n ∧
    ∃ f : Fin n → FreeGroup X, FreeGroup.lift f w = x}

instance verbalSubgroup_normal (V : GroupVariety) (X : Type u) : (V.verbalSubgroup X).Normal := by
  unfold verbalSubgroup
  infer_instance

/-- The relatively free group of rank `X` in the variety presented by `V`. -/
abbrev RelativelyFree (V : GroupVariety) (X : Type u) :=
  FreeGroup X ⧸ V.verbalSubgroup X

/-- A group is residually torsion-free nilpotent if each nonidentity element survives in some
torsion-free nilpotent quotient image. -/
def IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (N : Type u) (_ : Group N),
    Group.IsNilpotent N ∧ IsMulTorsionFree N ∧ ∃ φ : G →* N, φ g ≠ 1

/-- A group variety is soluble if all its members have derived length bounded by one common
natural number. -/
def IsSoluble (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], V.Satisfies G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥

/-- A presentation defines the variety of all groups if every group satisfies all its laws. -/
def IsAllGroups (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], V.Satisfies G

end GroupVariety

`V n` is a Lie polynomial in `n` variables required to equal zero. -/

end LieVariety

some fixed $n$. Varieties of Lie algebras are defined in the same way, using the free
Lie algebra on countably many generators.

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w`, an element of the free group on the countably many

`f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = 1

set of laws `W`, i.e. `G` satisfies every law in `W`. -/
def MemVariety (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesLaw G w

subgroup generated by all values `f w` of words `w ∈ W` under homomorphisms
`f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = g}

  Subgroup.normalClosure_normal

/-- The relatively free group $F_X(\mathfrak{V}) = F_X / W(F_X)$ of rank `X` in the variety
$\mathfrak{V} = \operatorname{Var}(W)$ of groups defined by the set of laws `W`. -/

  FreeGroup X ⧸ verbalSubgroup W (FreeGroup X)

  · intro h w hw f

    subst hw
    simp [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm, h]

kourovka.«4.72».why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), (∀ X : Type, IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (RelativelyFreeGroup W X)) → (∃ n, ∀ G, MemVariety W G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥) ∨ (∀ G, MemVariety W G)`. A variety is the class Var(W) of groups satisfying a set W of laws in the free group on x₀,x₁,… (H. Neumann's definition; Birkhoff-equivalent to S,H,C-closed classes). Its free groups are the relatively free groups F_X/W(F_X) of every rank X, residually (torsion-free nilpotent) is a per-element quotient condition, soluble means a uniform derived-length bound, and 'coincides with the variety of all groups' means every group is in Var(W).

kourovka.«4.72».variants.lie_algebras.why: Stated as the definite Prop: for every set W of identities in `FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ`, if no finite-dimensional `LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ` Lie algebra satisfies all identities in W, then there is a fixed n with `LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥` for every Lie algebra L over ℚ in the variety. Only the Lie-algebra claim is formalized; the implication to the group question is mentioned in the docstring but not asserted, per the decomposition table.

statement_blocks.kourovka.«4.72»:
/--
Is it true that every variety of groups whose free groups are residually nilpotent
torsion-free, is either soluble or coincides with the variety of all groups?

Here a variety is given by a set of laws `W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ`, its free groups are the
relatively free groups `RelativelyFreeGroup W X` of every rank `X`, "residually nilpotent
torsion-free" is read as residually (torsion-free nilpotent), and a variety is soluble if
there is a fixed `n` such that every group in the variety has derived length at most `n`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      (∀ X : Type, IsResiduallyTorsionFreeNilpotent (RelativelyFreeGroup W X)) →
        (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety W G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥) ∨
          (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety W G) := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.kourovka.«4.72».variants.lie_algebras:
/--
Every variety of Lie algebras over the field of rational numbers which does not contain any
finite-dimensional simple algebras is soluble.

Here a variety is given by a set of identities `W ⊆ FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ`, "simple" means
non-abelian with no non-trivial proper ideals (`LieAlgebra.IsSimple`), and a variety is
soluble if there is a fixed `n` such that every Lie algebra in the variety has derived
length at most `n`. According to the Kourovka Notebook, this statement implies an
affirmative answer to `kourovka.«4.72»`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.72».variants.lie_algebras :
    ∀ W : Set (FreeLieAlgebra ℚ ℕ),
      (∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ L]
        [LieAlgebra.IsSimple ℚ L], ¬ MemLieVariety ℚ W L) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℚ L],
          MemLieVariety ℚ W L → LieAlgebra.derivedSeries ℚ L n = ⊥ := by
  sorry
